title: <short human title>

commands.install: <install deps for every package, or "" if none — e.g. "cargo fetch && flutter pub get">
commands.test: <run every package's unit suite — e.g. "cargo test && flutter test">
commands.grade: <wrapper that runs every package's hidden grader and reports combined worst-case, living inside _solutions/ so the clone never carries it — e.g. "bash _solutions/grade.sh">

primaryBug: <one line: the silent, subset-only bug — for Cedar, its true cause lives across a boundary (reference/) and/or in a no-doc-trace stale path>

featureTrap.lure: <one line: how the brief reads as easy while leaning the obvious build onto the wrong rule>
featureTrap.naiveScore: <n>/<featureMax> — a naive one-shot build (fresh executor, brief raw); MUST fail the feature gate
featureTrap.elicitedScore: <n>/<featureMax> — an elicited or reference build; MUST pass the feature gate

assistantTrap: <one line: how an autopilot run provably loops — symptom-patch stays red; the obvious fix passes the visible suite but fails a case needing real understanding (FM-13, required)>
docDriftTrap: <one line: the authoritative-looking doc/comment that contradicts the current code, and the stale code path with no doc trace (FM-15)>
crossBoundaryTrap: <one line: the truth that lives only in reference/ and the wrong assumption a single-scope run makes (FM-16)>

controlRun.method: fresh assistant, harness-shaped clone (reference/ present, FEATURE-REQUEST.md held back), one casual uncoached prompt, no follow-up
controlRun.score: <n>/<max> — what an uncoached one-shot actually scores
controlRun.reference: <did it open reference/ unprompted? the FM-16 measurement>
controlRun.finding: <what the control run did and did not expose; if it clears the gate, say so and say what still discriminates>

notes: <anything a future maintainer needs — e.g. the dual grade gate or its single-stack fallback>
